title: SSE: ensure deterministic event ordering for partial-JSON + delimiter frames (fixes partial JSON, delimiter and token ordering)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Fix the SSE streaming framing edge cases that could emit delimiter events and token/event frames in a non-deterministic order, which caused downstream OpenAI-compat and streaming JSON parsers to see partial JSON objects in invalid sequences. Motivation: Customers observed sporadic parse errors and invalid partial JSON delivered to clients when streaming structured output or function/tool-calling events. Root cause: two race conditions: 1) delimiter lifecycle (open/close/partial markers) was driven by buffer flush timing separate from token/event serialization; 2) token-event ordering between token-chunk frames and higher-level event frames (e.g., 'tool.call' / 'tool.return') could interleave incorrectly when the transport flushed mid-event. Changes: - Serialize delimiter frames before token chunks at flush time to guarantee that a client that reconstructs JSON incrementally sees delimiter markers and opening/closing braces in order. - Introduce an explicit in-flight event queue in the SSE handler to preserve chronological ordering across flushes and across event types. - Add a small per-connection sequence counter used to enforce ordering during concurrent flushes; sequence values are only visible internally. - Fix the framing logic so partial-json tokens are emitted with a "partial_json":true attribute (OpenAI-compat layer) and the delimiter event is emitted immediately before any token events for that message. - Update the OpenAI compatibility shim to convert internal "delimiter" events to the expected "[DONE]"/"data: { ... }" ordering for clients using the OpenAI-style stream. - Add unit and e2e tests that reproduce the original race by forcing mid-message flushes and assert deterministic ordering. - Backported a minimal hotfix to release/2026-01 to mitigate ongoing customer incidents while we rolled out the full change. Testing: new unit tests, integration tests with the python and typescript compat clients, and a perf canary to ensure no regression in tail latency. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag `sse_strict_ordering` for staged rollout. Checklist: - [x] Repro case added as test - [x] Unit tests covering delimiter+token ordering - [x] OpenAI-compat shim updated - [x] Perf canary run (no tail-latency regression) - [x] Backport patch to release branch

release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming framing and ordering bug causing partial JSON parse errors in streaming OpenAI-compat clients. Included tests and a backport hotfix.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated by runtime flag `sse_strict_ordering`. Ops should enable on canary hosts and monitor sse_parse_errors and sse_tail_latency. Backport applied to release/2026-01 for customers experiencing incidents.
